algorithm_rules_2025_2026.summary: LinkedIn 2026 runs on an Interest Graph (not Social Graph). It matches content to TOPIC interest, not connections. Niche authority + dwell time + saves + meaningful comments are the top signals. External links, AI-sounding content, and engagement bait are suppressed.
key_changes: LinkedIn now prioritizes 'knowledge and advice' content over generic motivational posts
Niche content gets pushed to the RIGHT audience, not just the BIGGEST audience
External links are suppressed â€” keep content native to LinkedIn
Photos outperform videos on LinkedIn (opposite of Instagram/TikTok)
Text-only posts and text + single image posts get the most organic reach
Comments are weighted 2x+ MORE than reactions for algorithmic boost
Saves (bookmarks) are now the #1 quality signal â€” even above comments
The algorithm now detects and penalizes AI-generated content patterns
Interest Graph means your content reaches people interested in your TOPIC, not just your connections
Bridge behavior (funneling users to first comment for links) is increasingly detected and penalized
First 90 minutes after posting determine the post's trajectory
Posting 3-5 times per week is optimal (daily can hurt if quality drops)
The algorithm looks at 'dwell time' â€” how long someone spends reading your post
what_gets_suppressed: Posts with external links (put links in comments instead)
Engagement bait ('like if you agree', 'tag someone who...')
Posts that look AI-generated (perfect formatting, generic phrases, robotic repetition)
Bridge behavior â€” explicitly funneling users to first comment for a link
Engagement pods â€” LinkedIn's 2026 AI detection can shadowban accounts
Content that gets ignored in the first 90 minutes
what_gets_amplified: Posts that spark genuine conversation in comments
Native content (no outbound links in the post body)
Niche expertise posts that attract a specific professional audience
Personal stories with a clear professional takeaway
Posts where people spend time reading (dwell time)
Content from accounts that engage authentically with others' posts
Consistent posters who maintain quality (3-5x/week sweet spot)

formats.name: Brandjacking
formats.description: Attach your insight to a well-known brand, trend, or company. Borrow their recognition to amplify your message.
formats.how_it_works: Reference a recognizable brand/trend as the hook, then pivot to YOUR unique insight about it. The brand's name is the click-magnet.
formats.example_hook: Tesla just proved something most SaaS founders keep ignoring.
formats.key_mechanic: The Boomerang Effect â€” you throw attention at a big brand, and it boomerangs back to YOU because you provided the unique take.
formats.results: VP of Creative at Liquid Death engaging on a Brandjacking post

formats.name: Newsjacking
formats.description: Take breaking news or trending topics and add your expert angle within hours of the event.
formats.how_it_works: Speed matters. Be one of the first to provide an expert perspective on news your audience cares about.
formats.example_hook: Google I/O just announced [X]. Here's what no one is talking about.
formats.results: 208,000 impressions from a single Newsjacking post

formats.name: Namejacking
formats.description: Reference a well-known person (CEO, founder, thought leader) and react to their statement or idea.
formats.how_it_works: Quote or reference someone famous in your industry, then add your own take that either agrees, disagrees, or extends their idea.
formats.example_hook: Sam Altman said something last week that most founders missed.
formats.results: 147,000 impressions when Stephen Bartlett commented on a Namejacking post

formats.name: Hot Take
formats.description: Share a contrarian or bold opinion that challenges conventional wisdom in your niche.
formats.how_it_works: State a strong position that some people will disagree with. The disagreement drives comments, which drives the algorithm.
formats.example_hook: Unpopular opinion: Most 'AI startups' are just wrappers around ChatGPT.
formats.results: 390 comments and 300 reposts from one Hot Take post

pierre_herubel_method.core_principle: Get the right idea FIRST, then format well. 80% of a post's success is the idea, 20% is the writing.
idea_generation: Consume niche content daily (newsletters, podcasts, X/Twitter threads)
Keep an 'idea bank' â€” save every interesting insight you encounter
Reframe existing ideas through YOUR unique lens and experience
Ask: 'What do I know that most people in my industry don't?'
Look for 'so you can reuse it' â€” take one idea, express it in many formats
writing_rules: First 2 lines are EVERYTHING â€” they determine if people click 'see more'
One idea per sentence, one sentence per line
White space is your friend â€” break up text aggressively
Read your post out loud â€” if you stumble, rewrite
End with a question or a perspective, never a generic CTA

hook_formulas.description: Proven hook patterns that consistently drive 'see more' clicks on LinkedIn

patterns.name: Contrarian Statement
patterns.formula: [Widely accepted belief] is wrong. Here's why.
examples: Most founders are solving the wrong problem.
Your morning routine doesn't matter. Your systems do.
Stop building features. Start building distribution.

patterns.name: Curiosity Gap
examples: I deleted my entire tech stack last week. Revenue went up.
I stopped posting on LinkedIn for 30 days. Here's what happened.
I asked 50 founders one question. Same answer every time.

patterns.name: Pattern Interrupt
patterns.formula: [Shocking statement]. [Context that makes you want to read more].
examples: I got fired. Best thing that ever happened to my startup.
Google just made apps irrelevant. And nobody noticed.
The best code I ever wrote was the code I deleted.

patterns.name: Direct Authority
examples: 3 tools I actually use daily. Not hype. Not trendy.
208,000 impressions from one LinkedIn post. Here's the format.
We went from 0 to 5,000 users with zero ad spend.

patterns.name: Question Hook
patterns.formula: Why do [most people] [do X] when [Y is clearly better]?
examples: Why do most developers still build like it's 2020?
Why are founders still chasing features over distribution?
Why does nobody talk about the hardest part of building?

patterns.name: Newsjack Hook
patterns.formula: [Company/Person] just [did something]. [Your hot take in 1 line].
examples: Google just shipped something that changes everything for builders.
Sam Altman dropped a blog post. The real message is between the lines.
Claude just became a creative control center. Here's why that matters.

golden_rules: First 2 lines = your hook. They appear before 'see more'. Make them count.
Use line breaks generously (LinkedIn rewards readability)
Keep total post between 50-200 words for highest engagement
Longer posts (200-400 words) work for stories and case studies
Never exceed 400 words â€” LinkedIn truncates and people scroll past
Use numbered lists sparingly â€” max 3-5 items
Bullet points for technical breakdowns only
No more than 1-2 emojis per post (LinkedIn is professional)
Hashtags: 2-3 max, at the very end, relevant to topic
No external links in post body â€” put them in first comment
End with a question to drive comments (comments > reactions for algorithm)
visual_strategy: Personal photos > stock photos > AI images > no image
Selfies and behind-the-scenes photos build trust fastest
Screenshots of data/results perform well for credibility posts
Text-only posts often outperform image posts for thought leadership
Never use generic stock photography â€” it kills authenticity
If using an image, make sure it adds context, not just decoration

master_image_prompt_template.description: Use this template for EVERY LinkedIn post image. Replace the placeholder with a scene matching the post topic.
master_image_prompt_template.template: A vibrant flat vector illustration of [INSERT YOUR MAIN TOPIC/SCENE HERE]. The art style is quirky modern editorial with thin, uniform black outlines, and bright, highly saturated solid colors with no gradients. The characters have exaggerated proportions, rosy cheeks, dot eyes, and diverse appearances wearing fun patterned clothing. The composition is divided into a grid of multiple square and rectangular panels, each with a different brightly colored background. Crucially, the characters and objects are breaking the fourth wall by reaching across the panel borders to interact directly with the people and objects in the neighboring frames. Playful, dynamic, detailed.

posting_cadence.optimal_frequency: 3-5 times per week (Mon-Fri daily if quality can be maintained)
posting_cadence.best_times: Weekday mornings 8-10 AM IST, Tuesday-Thursday peak engagement, 10AM-12PM secondary window
posting_cadence.consistency_rule: A sustainable 3x/week beats an unsustainable daily schedule
posting_cadence.quality_over_quantity: One great post > three mediocre posts
posting_cadence.rest_days: Take weekends off â€” LinkedIn engagement drops significantly Sat/Sun

before_posting: Spend 10-15 minutes engaging with others' posts BEFORE publishing yours
Leave thoughtful comments (3+ sentences) on posts in your niche
This 'warms up' the algorithm and puts your profile in circulation
after_posting: Reply to EVERY comment within the first 90 minutes
Ask follow-up questions to commenters to keep the thread going
The first 90 minutes determine if the algorithm pushes your post wider
Pin the best/most insightful comment if LinkedIn allows it
comment_strategy: Comments on other people's posts are a growth engine
Treat every comment as a mini-post â€” add value, don't just agree
Comment on posts from people 1-2 levels above your audience size

common_mistakes: Posting external links directly (always put in comments — eordax rule)
Writing in AI voice (robotic, overly structured, generic)
Posting without a clear hook — most people never click 'see more'
Writing walls of text with no spacing or visual breaks
Being generic — LinkedIn rewards niche expertise, not broad advice
Posting inconsistently — algorithm rewards consistent creators
Ignoring comments — replying drives algorithmic push
Using too many hashtags (MAX 3, ideally 1-2 like eordax)
Copying trending formats without adding your own perspective
Posting motivational fluff without actionable insight
100% single-niche feed like Ghadeer — rotate across topic families
Zero personal/human content — at least 1 personal post per 5
Same hook opener pattern repeated (max 2x in 10 posts)
Follow/Repost/Save CTA footer (Ghadeer mistake) — use genuine questions
Same joke structure repeated like Rishabh's ChatGPT memes
Over-emoji decoration (🚀🔥💡✨ — use max 2-3 as punctuation)
Ending with generic 'Thoughts?' — ask specific questions instead
Posting without fresh research — must search_web for latest trends first
Same format every post — use 3+ formats per 7 posts (image, text, video, carousel)

profiles.name: Eduardo Ordax (eordax)
profiles.content_mix: 40% humor + 30% tool discovery + 20% deep takes + 10% personal
adopt_strategies: Tool discovery posts — find new GitHub repos/tools early, explain WHY not just WHAT
Links ALWAYS in first comment, never in post body
Ultra-minimal hashtags (1-2 max, usually just #ai)
Arrow lists with → for visual flow
Alert siren 🚨🚨🚨 for breaking discoveries
Mix formats: image + video + text-only in same week
Personal voice: 'My 2 cents...', 'I've been playing with it'
End with genuine question + 👇
avoid_patterns: 2-3 posts/day volume — too much for Ganesh's stage
Some posts are lazy reshares with no original thought

profiles.name: Ghadeer Al-Ruwaishedi
adopt_strategies: Contrarian flip hooks: 'Everyone says X. The opposite happened.'
Framework/mental model posts with named concepts
Data anchoring: cite McKinsey, specific percentages, real numbers
One sentence per line formatting for mobile readability
High comment ratio (avg 60+ comments) from discussion-driving questions
Data escalation pattern: Level 1 → Level 2 → Level 3 → Level 4
avoid_patterns: 100% AI niche — zero personal stories, zero humor, zero behind-the-scenes
Same 'Follow/Repost/Save' CTA footer on every post — BANNED
6 of 11 posts start with 'Everyone says X' — repetitive hook
100% image+text format — no variety (no text-only, no video, no carousel)
Some posts are 300+ words — over-long frameworks lose attention

profiles.name: Rishabh Jain
adopt_strategies: Ultra-short humor posts (≤50 words) — let the image carry the joke
Relatable irony: 'the thing you wanted becomes the problem you have'
Emoji as emotional punctuation (😂 😶 👀) not decoration
High share/tag behavior from humor posts
Mix text-only and image formats
avoid_patterns: 5+ hashtags per post — dilutes reach (MAX 3, ideally 1-2)
Zero depth — most posts have no learning takeaway
Repetitive ChatGPT joke structure (3 variations of same joke)
No build-in-public content — zero founder journey
No original thought — mostly reshared memes with no personal angle

profiles.name: Johnny C. Taylor Jr.
adopt_strategies: Multi-pillar content rotation — never stuck in one niche
Recurring 'Ask HR' column format — creates audience habit
Multi-audience targeting (executives, workers, students)
SHRM data/research anchoring for credibility
Signature series for weekly consistency
avoid_patterns: Corporate/institutional tone — too polished for Ganesh's builder voice

hard_block_anti_patterns: Zero personal content (min 1 personal/story per 5 posts)
Same format every post (min 3 formats in 7 posts)
Same hook opener more than 2x in 10 posts
Follow/Repost/Save CTA footer (end with genuine question)
Same joke structure repeated (context fingerprint dedup for humor)
Links in post body (ALWAYS put in first comment)
Over-emoji decoration (max 2-3 emojis, use as punctuation)
Copying exact post structure from inspiration profiles (adapt PATTERN only)
Posting without fresh research (must search_web first for latest trends)
